subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Is current G.711 u-law OpenAI realtime output plus the newer default model enough evidence to close this issue, or should maintainers require a fresh Twilio/OpenAI live repro before closing or changing the audio path?
rationale: Source and tests show the suspected conversion path is improved, but only live telephony audio can confirm the original first-30-seconds clipping behavior for the reported model/voice and carrier path.

options.title: Require Fresh Live Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a redacted v2026.6.11/current-main Twilio call or diagnostic log proves the failure boundary or confirms it no longer reproduces.

options.title: Close As Likely Covered
options.body: Close based on the shipped G.711 realtime path and newer model default, accepting that the original pinned model/voice was not re-tested live.

options.title: Land Instrumentation First
options.body: Ask for a narrow diagnostics PR that records output levels, queue depth, and provider audio format before deciding on gain or pacing changes.

recommendation.title: Require Fresh Live Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a redacted v2026.6.11/current-main Twilio call or diagnostic log proves the failure boundary or confirms it no longer reproduces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on OpenAI realtime defaults and voice-call pacing makes this the best available routing owner for the proof-sufficiency decision.
